candidates.title: Prepare a browser task outline for review

demandEvidence.chore: Control an existing browser from a terminal agent without interrupting the operator workflow.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: let the agent control your existing browser directly from the terminal without interrupting the workflow.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed sequence of browser actions for one operator-supplied, repeatable browser task.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a browser task that can be tested on a non-sensitive sample site.
steps: Turn the goal into a short action sequence.
List the expected page state after each action.
Compare the sequence with operator-provided screenshots or notes.
Revise ambiguous or unsafe actions for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a sample task, each proposed action matches the operator’s expected sequence and the final state is visibly verifiable.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies the goal and test site, reviews every action, and performs or authorizes any real browser action.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents browser control or agent execution.
Reliable page-state detection, permissions, and interruption behavior are unverified.
The source is a maker description, not evidence of repeat demand or payment.

ease.reason: A text outline can be drafted from an operator task, but no supplied source supports browser-control mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional service operators may pay to save time on repeated browser work; this maker post proves no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week sample-site outline test is possible, while reliable browser state and action execution are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop drafts steps only; a person must execute and verify them because browser automation is undocumented.

evidence.reason: The post states a browser-control use case, but provides no demonstrated use, external request, or corroborated demand.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: this is a maker description of browser control, and no supplied implementation reference supports the proposed action loop.

candidates.title: Plan a guarded workflow repair

demandEvidence.chore: Plan restoration of one missing node and its two connections while preserving the rest of an inactive workflow.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Only the missing node and its two connections should be restored.

experimentPlan.output: A pre-change checklist comparing a proposed one-node repair with an operator-supplied workflow snapshot and backup.
inputs: Synthetic workflow node and connection list
Synthetic backup node and connection list
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator requests review of a narrowly described missing-node repair using fictional workflow data.
steps: Compare the current and backup node lists.
Identify the single proposed node and its two proposed connections.
List workflow properties that must remain unchanged.
Generate a checklist of differences and unresolved questions.
Ask a human to verify the checklist against the real workflow before any edit.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For synthetic fixtures, the checklist identifies the intended node and connections and flags every deliberately introduced unrelated change.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A human supplies and validates the snapshots, decides whether a repair is safe, performs any real edit, and confirms the result; no credentials or live workflow access are used.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports n8n version behavior, concurrency protection, or safe workflow edits.
The exact node configuration and connection semantics are unverified.
Synthetic comparisons do not establish safe execution or persistence in n8n.

ease.reason: A beginner can compare fictional node and connection lists, but the post gives no supported repair procedure.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: workflow consultants may pay for repair planning; this single request establishes no payment or repeat buyer demand.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic checklist test is scoped, though real version behavior and safe edits remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable comparison can flag differences, but a human must validate and apply every real change.

evidence.reason: The retained post spans specify a missing node, two connections, preservation constraints, and uncertainty about safe updates; no implementation evidence is supplied.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: fresh retained spans specify a concrete repair task, but no implementation source supports safe or version-specific changes.

candidates.title: Prepare a warm-introduction matching brief

demandEvidence.chore: Find business partners who can make warm introductions to decision-makers with operational problems.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: introduce me to the right ones: companies with a real operational problem

experimentPlan.output: A human-reviewed shortlist of partner categories and introduction questions from operator-supplied business descriptions.
inputs: Consent status for any real introduction
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies fictional descriptions and asks for possible partner-to-business matches.
steps: Extract only business category and stated problem from each fictional record.
Draft a short reason for each suggested match.
Flag missing consent or insufficient information.
Have a person approve any real outreach or introduction.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fictional test set, every suggested match satisfies the operator-defined criteria and includes no unsupported contact detail.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies lawful, consented information and criteria, reviews every match, and makes or authorizes any introduction; no personal profiles or contact details are collected.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports matching or outreach automation.
The post gives no matching criteria, repeat frequency, or evidence that a shortlist tool is wanted.
Any payer remains hypothetical; the author’s revenue-share offer does not verify buyer demand.

ease.reason: A fictional matching brief is easy to outline, but no source documents matching or outreach tools.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent consultants may pay for partner matching; the post requests introductions but does not establish tool buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week fictional matching exercise is possible, but criteria and recurring volume are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: The proposal can suggest matches only; a human must verify fit, consent, and every introduction.

evidence.reason: The retained span explicitly asks for warm introductions to business decision-makers, but supplies no repeat workflow or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the request is for warm introductions, but a repeatable software workflow and buyer for a matching service are unsubstantiated.
